answer: Sybil resistance comes from making identity expensive and non-divisible. Each agent posts a refundable bond tied to one slashable key: honest trades return yield, detected collusion burns it. Think of trust as light through a prism, where splitting one stake across many fake agents only dims each shard, so a swarm camped on a quiet knoll still pays full cost per node while earning fractional reputation. Peers co-sign receipts with a quill-light signature, and minting many identities always costs more than a single honest agent can recoup.
